name: Prone Y-Raise (Thumbs Up)
description: The prone Y-raise performed with thumbs pointing upward (externally rotated shoulders) on a flat surface trains the lower trapezius through its primary action of upward scapular rotation and depression. The external rotation (thumbs up) is critical — it places the shoulder in its safest overhead position and maximally lengthens the lower trapezius before each repetition, improving the exercise's effectiveness as both a strengthening and postural correction tool.

execution.starting_position: Lie face down on a bench or the floor. Arms extended in a Y position (45 degrees overhead from the spine). Thumbs pointing toward the ceiling.
execution.setup_instructions: Bodyweight or 1-2 kg per hand. The movement is fully achievable without weight for most people.
steps: Step 1: Begin lying prone, arms in Y position, thumbs up.
Step 2: Raise both arms toward the ceiling while maintaining the Y angle and thumbs-up rotation.
Step 3: Squeeze the lower traps — think 'shoulder blades toward the back pockets'.
Step 4: Hold 2 seconds at the top.
common_mistakes: Thumbs rotating down — this internally rotates the shoulder and reduces lower trap activation
Arms going overhead (beyond Y) — the angle must be maintained
safety_considerations: Bodyweight appropriate for all fitness levels
Very light optional load — this is a rehabilitation and activation drill
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Floor-level to arms raised with scapulae fully depressed and retracted.
coaching_cues: Thumbs point to the ceiling throughout
Shoulder blades pull toward your back pockets
